**Commit**: `8853f74a5386` — docs(sweep): post-merge triage — the fence landed, the template's own correctness did not

**Body**:

Second sweep of the day. The morning one ranked the proposal above PR #80; both have since
landed, so this triages what remains — including four filings that sweep never saw.

THE FINDING THAT REORDERS THE QUEUE: the completion gap moved from the fence to the TEMPLATE
ITSELF. Three verified defects mean a consumer following the documented contract today
deletes shipped files (#78 — all five listed paths confirmed present AND listed obsolete),
loads a priority-0 baseline rule whose cited authority does not exist (#79 — verified at
ELEVEN citing files, not the five filed), and can have locally-codified rules destroyed on
sync with no preservation path (#64 — both contradicting lines still present at 2.24.0, and
no rules/project/ or commands/project/ home exists).

Every claim was verified mechanically before triage rather than taken from the issue body.
Two of the four filings resolved that way: #76 is fixed (its own regression lock passes
17/17) and #74's diagnosis was wrong (the guard blocks correctly when coordination is ON;
measured both lanes). #74's OBSERVATION was real and is carved out as #89 rather than closed
with it — a harness that asserts the wrong precondition on a security fixture will produce
that false alarm again.

Two decision points surfaced rather than self-decided. D1: #86 and #87 are the same proposal
at the same inbox path and disagree on exactly the reachability question #86 flags for
template judgement — merge order must not decide it. D2: #78/#79 are defects in SYNCED
artifacts, so a local fix is Class-A non-durable; recommending both a labelled stopgap and
the proposal, because #78 is actively destructive to consumers pulling today.

Sweep-N returns EMPTY for the second consecutive sweep, and again not because the backlog is
clear: the deferred-quality label and issue template still do not exist, so no INCREMENTAL
item can be deferred compliantly per product-completion-first MUST-2.
